title: Heavy periods: reducing bleeding and checking anemia
intro: Menstrual bleeding is heavy when its amount or duration disrupts life, not only when it meets a measured volume. It may cause iron deficiency and fatigue. You do not need to prove a precise blood loss before asking for help.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Frequent product changes, flooding, large clots or avoiding work and outings can indicate a problem. Fibroids, adenomyosis, hormonal changes and bleeding disorders are possible causes; bleeding between periods needs separate attention.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: Describe the pattern, pregnancy possibility, medicines and bleeding elsewhere. A blood count checks anemia; further tests or ultrasound depend on history and examination. Discuss consent and comfort before intimate examinations. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Options may include tranexamic acid, suitable anti-inflammatory medicines, hormonal contraception or a hormonal intrauterine system. Procedures depend on the cause and preferences; future pregnancy plans matter before treatments that affect fertility. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Track bleeding and symptoms in a simple diary and discuss iron replacement when deficient. Choose comfortable products and practical workplace support. Do not assume persistent exhaustion is normal or start several medicines without checking contraindications. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Very heavy ongoing bleeding with faintness, breathlessness, chest pain or collapse requires urgent help. Possible pregnancy with pain or bleeding needs prompt assessment. New bleeding after menopause should not be treated as another ordinary period.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira avoids leaving home during periods. She describes the disruption and fatigue, leading to anemia testing and discussion of treatment rather than simply stronger pads.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben supports a partner in recording symptoms and arranging a visit. She discusses future pregnancy before choosing a procedure that may affect fertility.
